title: Recursive Model Improvement — Lee Robinson, Cursor, SpaceXAI
talk_summary: Lee Robinson describes Cursor's model-training flywheel: an outer loop of user feedback/AB tests feeding evals, and an inner loop of hard verifiable RL tasks, textual-feedback credit assignment, and derivative models that judge/reward.

takeaways.evidence_quote: we would delete the Git history at the start, and we could restore it at the end
takeaways.numbers: a couple small changes produced a noticeable change in reported scores

takeaways.technique: Private held-out eval set from real work
takeaways.what_they_do: They maintain Cursor Bench: a private eval of real codebase tasks held out from training, because public benchmarks don't reflect real usage.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We have this private eval set that is mostly made up of things that happen in our code base

takeaways.technique: Retire saturated evals, generate harder ones by deletion
takeaways.what_they_do: They retire evals when all models hit ~90%, and auto-generate hard tasks by taking a working app, deleting a feature/files so tests fail, and asking the model to reimplement until tests pass.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can delete a feature, you can delete files and the test will then fail

takeaways.technique: Agent fleet with human paging on failure
takeaways.what_they_do: Every ML researcher gets a fleet of agents they launch from Slack; agents run long experiments and message/page the human only when infra breaks or something important happens.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the model can message them on Slack or just page them directly

takeaways.technique: Textual feedback for localized credit assignment
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of grading only at rollout end, they zoom into one step, add a hint ('you have these tools available'), and up/down-weight probabilities for that behavior.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we want to zoom in on one specific part of that rollout, and ideally we can hint

takeaways.technique: Automate the non-creative parts of the loop
takeaways.what_they_do: A dedicated team automates every part of research that isn't the researcher's most ambitious idea, so humans aren't bottlenecked launching/reviewing/babysitting runs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We want to avoid this state of being bottlenecked on humans launching and reviewing and babysitting runs
